newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. newspaper editorials - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. newspaper editorials - Oct 16.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press Wednesday. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 258 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe who escaped from China and was on his way to the United States, and other domestic issues.

-- The middle of the road MING PAO DAILY NEWS said that it was sad to see a patriotic intellectual such as Wang Xizhe being forced to leave the country. It said that although Wang criticised the government a lot, it was obvious that he had deep affection for Chnna. It said there were many such intellectuals in China and if they were allowed to stay there and contribute to the country's future, China would be a lot different.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that Hong Kong would no longer be the refuge and gateway for Chinese dissidents after the 1997 handover. What is at stake is how those who have "collaborated" with dissidents from the mainland will be treated after 1997. It said this meant that a key issue in the handover remained worryingly unresolved. It said if what people did today was held as a sword over their heads tomorrow, the rule of law would be seriously impaired.

-- SING TAO DAILY said that Japan would not hand back the disputed Diaoyu Islands to China willingly and the dispute might have to go to international court and be settled according to international law. It said that because China had already had legal evidence of its sovereignty over the islands, it should be able to win the case.
